title: Static Open Bird Hatch and Hanging Weight Clock
description: One wholly newly authored complete fixed bird-window wall-clock exterior. A full deep timber case has a true upper blind bird chamber and one thick hatch held open on its fixed hinge; one whole small stylized bird rests on a continuous short perch projecting from the chamber back. Below are a complete raised circular bezel, recessed ivory dial, twelve plain markers and two separately layered fixed hands. One full pendulum rod and bob plus two continuous suspension-appearance cords and two whole shaped weights hang below the case. A full thick gabled cap closes the top. Unlike the old open-frame table clock or four-faced through-arch tower, this whole shallow wall case organises an actual opening bird compartment above the dial and separate hanging pendulum/weight elements below it; no old clock, roof or bird mesh imported. Three opaque constant PBR roles, metres Z-up, full horizontal bounds-centred origin at the lowest weight bottoms. One static uninstalled wall prop zero scenes. No host wall or load-bearing mount is supplied; the hanging display pose is fixed geometry, not a demonstrated supported installation. No working internal escapement, bird linkage, bellows, chime, timekeeping, calibration, pendulum motion, cord winding, moving hatch, manufacture or safety capability. Small bird is a simplified ornament, not biological anatomy. Rigging animation interaction not made.
